'''Anton Amann''' (20 June 1956 – 6 January 2015) was an [[Austria]]n [[chemist]] and 
[[Professor]] of [[chemistry]] at the [[Innsbruck Medical University]].       
He worked in the area of physical chemistry, ECG analysis, and [[breath gas analysis|exhaled breath analysis]].

Amann was the head of the Breath Research Institute of the [[University of Innsbruck|Leopold-Franzens University of Innsbruck]] (formerly an Institute of the Austrian Academy of Science) and editor in chief of the Journal of Breath Research.<ref>[http://iopscience.iop.org/1752-7163/page/Editorial%20Board Editorial Board, Journal of Breath Research]</ref>

He authored more than 150 scientific articles.<ref>[http://www.voc-research.at/index.php/selected-publications Selected Publications] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706095349/http://www.voc-research.at/index.php/selected-publications |date=July 6, 2011 }}</ref> He died in Innsbruck in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://traueranzeigen.tt.com/traueranzeige/2101895-univ-prof-dr-anton-amann.html|title=Univ.-Prof. Dr. Anton Amann|date=6 January 2015|publisher=traueranzeigen.tt.com|language=German}}</ref>

==Career==

After studying [[chemistry]] at the [[ETH Zürich]], he continued with a [[PhD]] in Science. The title of his dissertation 1984 with [[Hans Primas]] and [[Norbert Straumann]] was ''Observable in der W*-algebraischen Quantenmechanik'' ([[observable]]s in [[W*-algebra]]ic [[quantum mechanics]]).<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=141721 | title=Anton Amann - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> In 1991 he earned [[Habilitation]] in Physical Chemistry at the ETH Zürich. From 1987 to 1995 he was a senior research associate at the Institute of Physical Chemistry at the ETH Zürich.

In 1995 he was awarded an APART grant from the Austrian Academy of Sciences and he also received an invitation to join Yale University as associate professor. In 1993 he was awarded with AECI Gold Medal by the South African Chemical Institute. In 2010, he received the [[Marie Curie Medal]] of the [[Polish Chemical Society]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ptchem.pl/pl/honors/winners-of-the-medals-and-ptchem-awards |title=Laureaci Medali i Nagród PTChem |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref>

From 2006 to 2009 he was the coordinator of the European Union Project BAMOD <ref>{{Cite web |title=Breath-gas analysis for molecular-oriented detection of minimal diseases {{!}} BAMOD {{!}} Projekt {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} FP6 {{!}} CORDIS ! European Commission |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/19031/factsheet |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref> (lung carcinoma screening, project funding: 3 million euro). In 2005 he was chairman and organizer of the international conference ''Breath Analysis for Clinical Diagnosis and Therapeutic Monitoring''.,<ref>[http://www.voc-research.at/images/innsbruck_2005.pdf 2005 conference]{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Innsbruck]] (Austria). In 2004 he was chairman and organizer of the international conference ''Breath Gas Analysis for Medical Diagnostics''.,<ref>[http://www.voc-research.at/images/dornbirn_2004.pdf 2004 conference]{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Dornbirn]] (Austria).

Since 1997 he was a professor of chemistry at the [[University of Innsbruck|Leopold-Franzens University of Innsbruck]], and since 2004 at the [[Innsbruck Medical University]].
